results.name: Lying Glute Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left knee, forming a figure-four position.
Grasp the back of your left thigh with both hands and gently pull your left leg towards your chest. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your right glute and hip.
Slowly release your left leg and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left ankle crossed over your right knee. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor to avoid tension in your neck and upper back.
Avoid pulling too hard; go as far as your flexibility allows without causing pain.
Use a towel or strap if needed to assist in pulling your leg towards your chest.
results.description: Lying Glute Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lying Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight on the floor.
Lift your right knee towards your chest, holding it with both hands to keep it close while extending your left leg straight off floor, keeping it in line with your right foot.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release your right knee and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch with your left knee lifted towards your chest and your right leg extended. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your lower back pressed into the floor to avoid strain and to deepen the stretch.
Start with a smaller range of motion if you feel any discomfort, gradually increasing as flexibility improves.
Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you prepare for the stretch and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
results.description: Lying Hip Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

results.name: Lying Knee Hugs Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back.
Pull both knees toward your chest.
Wrap your arms around your shins and hug them in.
Hold, breathing slowly, and relax your lower back into the floor.
tips: Rock gently side to side for a light massage.
Keep your head on the floor.
results.description: Lying Knee Hugs Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Lying Knee Pull Glutes Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your legs straight.
Bend one knee and pull it toward the opposite shoulder.
Hold until you feel a stretch in your glute.
Release and switch sides.
tips: Keep the other leg relaxed on the floor.
Breathe deeply.
results.description: Lying Knee Pull Glutes Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

results.name: Lying Knees to Floor Lower Back Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and arms out to the sides.
Keeping your shoulders on the floor, lower both knees to one side.
Hold, feeling a stretch in your lower back and side.
Bring your knees back to the centre and lower them to the other side.
tips: Turn your head away from your knees for a deeper stretch.
Move slowly.
results.description: Lying Knees to Floor Lower Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes.

results.name: Lying Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Lie face down on the floor with your legs extended straight and your arms resting by your sides.
Bend your right knee and reach back with your right hand to grasp your right ankle or foot.
Gently pull your right foot towards your glutes, feeling the stretch in your right quadriceps. Keep your hips pressed into the floor.

Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly release your right foot and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on your left leg. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips pressed into the floor to maximize the stretch in your quadriceps and avoid straining your lower back.
Move slowly and with control to avoid any sudden movements that could cause strain.
If you cannot reach your foot comfortably, use a towel or strap around your ankle to assist with the stretch.
results.description: Lying Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lying Side Quadriceps Stretch
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs extended straight and your head resting on your lower hand. Extend your top arm and reach back to grasp your top ankle or foot.
Bend your top knee and gently pull your foot towards your glutes with your hand, feeling the stretch in your quadriceps. Keep your hips stacked and your body in a straight line.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily.
Slowly release your foot and return to the starting position. Repeat the stretch on the other side. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips stacked and your body in a straight line to maintain proper alignment and maximize the stretch.
If you cannot reach your foot comfortably, use a towel or strap around your ankle to assist with the stretch.
Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you prepare for the stretch and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
results.description: Lying Side Quadriceps Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Lying Single Leg Extended on Wall Hamstrings Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back in a doorway or next to a wall.
Place one leg straight up against the wall, the other flat on the floor.
Move closer to the wall until you feel a stretch in the back of the raised leg.
Hold, then switch legs.
tips: Keep both legs straight.
Relax your shoulders and neck.
results.description: Lying Single Leg Extended on Wall Hamstrings Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Middle Back Rotation Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart and your hands placed on your hips.
Slowly rotate your torso to the right, keeping your hips facing forward. Twist as far as is comfortable, feeling the stretch in your middle back.
Return to the center and repeat the rotation to the right once more.
Rotate your torso to the left side twice in the same manner, alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your hips facing forward to ensure the stretch targets your middle back effectively.
Perform the stretch on a stable, non-slip surface to prevent slipping or discomfort.
Avoid forcing the twist; go as far as your flexibility allows without causing pain.
results.description: Middle Back Rotation Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

results.name: Overhead Triceps Stretch (45 Degree View)
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Raise your right arm overhead and bend your elbow, reaching your right hand down towards your upper back.
Bring your left arm overhead and hold your right elbow with your left hand, gently pulling your right elbow to the left side to deepen the stretch. Hold this position for 15-30 seconds.

Release the stretch and return to the starting position. Repeat on the left side by raising your left arm overhead and bending your elbow, using your right hand to assist with the stretch. Alternate sides for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid arching your back; keep your spine neutral to maximize the stretch and prevent injury.
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and support your lower back.
Use gentle pressure when pulling on your elbow to avoid overstretching and potential discomfort.
results.description: Overhead Triceps Stretch (45 Degree View) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.
